explanation: Glands near its nose collect salt from the blood, and the iguana blasts it out in sneezes, often leaving its head crusted white.

claims.text: Marine iguanas, which live in the Galápagos and eat seaweed, get rid of excess salt by sneezing it out of glands near the nostrils.
Marine iguanas do not mainly get rid of salt by shedding skin, through tears or by sweating.
Salt sneezed out by marine iguanas often leaves a white crust on their heads.
